title: Competitive runway calculator and signal-integrated model-availability playbook
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Background: As open-model availability becomes more bursty and regional, product and procurement teams need a repeatable way to translate live signals (provider outages, release cadence, quantization adoption, price shocks, reserved capacity commitments) into procurement and routing actions. This ticket builds a lightweight 'runway calculator' that synthesizes heterogeneous signals into a probabilistic availability window and a set of recommended mitigation actions (reserve, fallback model, regional routing, burst capacity).

Goals: 1) Produce a decision-ready calculator that outputs: days-of-runway by region/model-class, primary risk drivers, and a ranked set of tactical mitigations with estimated cost/latency impact. 2) Publish a playbook for Sales/CS/Platform to act on the calculator outputs (procurement thresholds, alerting rules, and ownership handoffs). 3) Integrate with monitoring dashboards and a simple Confluence playbook for runbooks and exec summaries.
acceptance_criteria: Calculator accepts region, model family (e.g., Llama-like, MPT-like), current usage profile (QPS and token mix), and outputs days-of-runway with 3 probability tiers (P50/P10/P90)
Calculator surfaces top-3 risk drivers per region and maps each to a recommended mitigation (reserve capacity, route to variant, throttle noncritical traffic, prewarm cache)
Playbook contains clear action thresholds (e.g., <14 days P10 triggers procurement engagement; <7 days P10 triggers canary capacity purchases) and owner assignments
Integration: calculator outputs ingested into console-ops dashboard as a card and into an internal Slack alerting channel with links to the playbook
Doc + one pager: Confluence playbook and an exec-facing slide summarizing methodology and tradeoffs
tasks: Define input signals & weighting heuristic (owner: Ethan) - catalog provider status feeds, latency SLO breach rates, reserved capacity commitments, price change events
Prototype statistical model for runway estimation (owner: Research - Liaison: Marcus Patel)
Build a lightweight REST endpoint returning JSON runway estimates (owner: Eng: Keiko Tan)
Wire console card & Slack alerting (owner: Platform Eng)
Draft Confluence playbook and 1-pager with thresholds and escalation paths (owner: Priya)
Stakeholder review and tabletop runbook drill with Sales and SRE (owner: Ethan)
Post-mortem calibration plan: capture outcomes and refine heuristics after first 2 months
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with SRE, Procurement and Sales. Confirmed access to provider-status feeds and billing change webhooks.
2025-02-20: Weighting heuristic v0 drafted (latency breach 40%, provider outage frequency 30%, reserved GPU queue time 20%, price shock velocity 10%). Shared with Research for simulation.
2025-02-28: Prototype estimator returns plausible runway windows in synthetic tests. Eng scaffold for REST endpoint created (PR #12 open).
2025-03-03: Stakeholder review scheduled; drafted playbook with initial thresholds. Added tabletop drill to scope for 2025-W11.
risks: Signal quality: provider status feeds are noisy and vary by region — risk of false positives leading to unnecessary procurement
Model drift: early heuristics may under/over-estimate runway — requires post-hoc calibration
Operational friction: agreed thresholds may require new cross-team SLAs for procurement lead times
Cost sensitivity: recommended mitigations could materially increase unit cost if invoked frequently
decisions: Use a heuristic + calibration approach rather than a fully Bayesian model for first iteration to prioritize explainability
Expose P10/P50/P90 bands and recommend actions off P10 to bias toward conservative procurement when customer impact is high
Playbook actions will be triaged by severity and team: Procurement (reserve buys), Platform (regional routing), DevRel/Sales (customer communication)
